questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The combination of being able to explore New Zealand as it is very far away and I won't just get another chance to visit as well as the university having great academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Overall the  University  of Otago was really good at guiding their exhange students (As they also receive quite a few international students)

Very easy to get from airport to the office where I got my key to my house and they even drove me to my house afterwards even though I arrived in the evening (All arranged by the university)

Furthermore there were a lot of events to get to know other international students as well as getting to know the university and life in New Zealand that upcoming week

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a little problem with a fee regarding some of my courses, but I asked AskOtago upon arrival and they were very nice and helped me with my issue

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy - Almost all of their housing were located next to the university and they even drove me to my house when I arrived (Even though it was a couple hundred meters from the key pick up spot)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Great opportunity to meet other exhange students. Living off campus is close to living on campus (In Dunedin) but you get more freedom as you have your "own" house thta you share with other students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some trouble figuring out how to applu but after looking at AskOtago and writing an email to the university I figured out how to apply correctly

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get contacted by an employer from the host university who gives you a list and a guide on how to do it. The list I got was a bit outdated so a had a bit of difficulties in the beginning, but was able to find the answers to all of my questions on their website and through AskOtago or by sending an email to the university (The contact-employ wasn't of much help though)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The possibility to write to the university itself. Furtermore their website is packed with information as well

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: You get contacted by an employer from the host university who gives you a list and a guide on how to do it. The list I got was a bit outdated so a had a bit of difficulties in the beginning, but was able to find the answers to all of my questions on their website and through AskOtago and all my classes were accepted (Both from KU and Otago)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: AskOtago! I didn't have any luck contacting the employee who sent me the email with the information, but when I contacted the university through another mail they were very kind to help. Otherwise try and contact some of the other people from your university who are going to the same place (if there are any)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved my classes there

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A fitting level - Some classes I took were quite demanding whereas other were more standard level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar in lecture style, but they had a bit more laboratory work but less group work in regular class rooms (Holdundervisning)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANAT242: Neurobiology
GENE313: Medical Genetics
MICR223: Infection and Immunity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I loved ANAT242 but I also really wanna do something relating to neuroscience.
If you are more into genetics I would also really recommend GENE313 as you get to do some more laboratory stuff than what I at least am used to (Same with MICR223)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not unexpected but be aware that you often need to pay an insurance through your host university even though you already have travel insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were a bit more expensive that anticipated (They often need to import some of the vegetables that we are used to having here in Denmark)
The local bus were so much cheaper than what I am used to in CPH - It costs around 4DKK to take the bus as long as you want in one direction (If you are a student or under 25).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs & associations etc. available through the university (The price varied from club to club) - These clubs were both cultural, athletic, social and creative. Furthermore there was a free gym were you could also play badminton, volleyball, basket ball etc. for free.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Explore the nature around you - New Zealand is so beautiful
Also, join one of the clubs, as it is a good way to meet new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Milford Sound
Wanaka
Kaikoura
Catlins National Park
Wellington
Mt. Cook
Tongariro National Park

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, it is not that different but still is more focused on different cultures (through the Maori culture) than in Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: For me it work by just talking to them in class. Sit next to someone and say hi - Sometimes it is hard especially in lectures, but when you have laboratory hours (or something similar) try starting a conversation. It is easier here as you most likely also need to discuss some groupwork. Otherwise see if there is a local arrangement or market going on.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It seemed quite including

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Don't be afraid to ask people if they want to grab a cup of coffee or go with you on a trip - Exchange is much more fun if you have someone to share it with (Either locals or other exchange students)

2) Exchange is both about school but also exploring a new country

3) But also remember that you are going to be there for a longer time than a regular vacation, so if you feel overwhelmed/stressed or just not feeling it, it is still okay to say no to plans

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, just enjoy:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know myself better in a new setting and while on my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The hardest part were right in the beginning when I left friends and family at home and had no idea what to expect upon arrival. Luckily I had some sweet sweet flatmates and already felt great after the first week.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
